question: A 25-year-old woman presents to the physician with a complaint of several episodes of headaches in the past 4 weeks that are affecting her school performance. These episodes are getting progressively worse, and over-the-counter medications do not seem to help. She also mentions having to raise her head each time to look at the board while taking notes; she cannot simply glance up with just her eyes. She has no significant past medical or family history and was otherwise well prior to this visit. Physical examination shows an upward gaze palsy and convergence-retraction nystagmus. What structure is most likely to be affected in this patient?
analysis: The patient's symptoms of headaches, upward gaze palsy, and convergence-retraction nystagmus are indicative of a condition known as Parinaud syndrome, which is typically caused by a lesion in the dorsal midbrain. The structure most likely affected in this patient is the Corpora quadrigemina, specifically the superior colliculi.
